name: Malchus
overview: Malchus was a male servant of the high priest during the time of Jesus' arrest. He is specifically noted in Scripture as the high priest's slave whose ear was cut off by the apostle Peter. Beyond this unique event, there is little additional information about his background or tribe.
namesAndTitles: The name Malchus is a proper name meaning 'king.' This meaning is noted in the Gospel of John 18:10, though the name was not given by God. The name itself does not carry further recorded significance in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Malchus beyond his role as the high priest's slave, as indicated in his unique attribute. No other relationships are listed or known.
scriptureSignificance: Malchus is significant in the biblical narrative as the individual directly affected by Peter's impulsive act during Jesus' arrest. His ear being cut off highlights the tension and violence surrounding the betrayal of Christ, and this event also sets the stage for Jesus' demonstration of mercy and healing. Malchus' presence helps illustrate the personal cost of the unfolding redemptive plan.
